title: Desktop 0.2.0 prerelease published on GitHub Releases
summary: The Rust engine's desktop 0.2.0 build, made from main commit edfc4aa, is a GitHub prerelease for macOS (universal), Linux (x86_64 and aarch64) and Windows (x86_64). It adds the Rust frontend with Select Track and Select ATV & Rider, remappable key and controller bindings, Crazy/Gorn crashes, deterministic simulation maths on every platform, and motorcycles in Freeride with their particles, mud and sound. It is an unsigned early preview, not the finished game.
details: Release: https://github.com/nrgapple/atv-offroad-fury-2-web/releases/tag/desktop-v0.2.0-edfc4aa (marked prerelease). Four archives of about 418-423 MB each (macOS universal zip, Linux x86_64 and aarch64 tar.gz, Windows x86_64 zip) plus SHA256SUMS.txt. The runtime resources the port needs are packed into each archive, so no disc, emulator or install step is needed. Built locally from edfc4aa with tools/build_desktop.py; every archive passed the member allowlist and a full re-hash of the packed content, and none contains the ISO, BIOS, boot executable or private files.

What edfc4aa ships (PR numbers): #206 remappable keyboard and controller bindings and controller settings, saved in the browser's formats; #210 the Rust frontend (title, main menu, single player, Select Track for all 40 venues with the original course photos, Select ATV & Rider for all 46 vehicles, the course loader with the original action shots and tips, Pause > Quit to Main Menu), measured against play.html at 1.18/255 (1280x720) and 1.98/255 (390x844) mean absolute RGB on Select Track; #207 Crazy/Gorn crashes and Gorn blood; #208 deterministic simulation maths, so web, macOS, Windows and Linux play identical inputs bit for bit (a 9,000-step ENV01 race matches JavaScript, Rust browser and native macOS at every step; the headless fingerprints are identical on macOS aarch64, Linux aarch64 and Linux x86_64; CI now checks six targets); #209 motorcycles in Freeride (bike physics, rider, camera and HUD identical to the JavaScript game at every compared step); #211 motorcycle particles and mud (held-frame vehicle-box difference against the JavaScript game 6.19 before, 0.13 browser and 0.15 native after); #212 motorcycle sound (all 13 engine samples play in the same order within 1-6 steps; 100 ms levels within 0.70 dB mean), and the ATV engine and rider vocals now follow the Garage choice.

Not in this desktop build: #214 (3D quad and rider previews in the menus) and #215 (motorcycle races, whose 9,000-step bike race matches the JavaScript game bit for bit) merged after edfc4aa. They are live on the preview page https://furyremastered.com/engine.html (deployment.json reports commit dbb62be) and will reach desktop in the next build. In 0.2.0 the desktop Main, Single Player and Garage pages therefore show no 3D vehicle or rider previews, and motorcycles can only be ridden in Freeride, not raced. play.html remains the main JavaScript game.

Desktop 0.2.0 verification: the macOS universal app was unzipped and its code signature verified; --version reports 0.2.0; --verify-content checked 219 files / 454 MB in 2.1 s; an SX01 motorcycle ride and the Select Track menu were captured and inspected (the Intel half was built but not run, and the Metal run was on Apple silicon). Linux aarch64 launched to the title screen in Docker (Debian 12, Xvfb, Mesa lavapipe software Vulkan) in 6.1 s, and Linux x86_64 did the same under emulation in 22.6 s. No real Linux GPU or audio device was tried. Windows x86_64 was built and structurally checked but not run.
limitation: Unsigned, unnotarized builds (macOS Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen warn on first launch). Windows was never run. Missing in the desktop app: multiplayer, progression, race music, start lamps and fireworks. Desktop-versus-browser menu parity was not measured for 0.2.0, and no real-GPU Linux results exist. This is an incomplete fan port; the browser game still has the most complete feature set.
